sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: PI-PLC release confirms GPI-anchored surface display; proteolytic activity preserved as shown by TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 inhibition assays; TIMP-2 complex formation confirmed.
sites.rationale: MMP25 is a GPI-anchored protein with no transmembrane domain; the entire ectodomain (residues 22–562) is extracellular. The C-terminus carries the GPI anchor signal sequence (cleaved and replaced by the GPI lipid moiety), making it unavailable for tagging. Therefore exactly one free extracellular terminus exists — the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 22 — and the FLAG tag must reside there, inserted after the signal peptide cleavage site at residue 21 (A). Python verification confirms canonical_seq[21]='A' and canonical_seq[22]='P', consistent with the landmarks. FLAG-tagged full-length MT6-MMP (MMP25) expressed in MCF-7 breast carcinoma and HT1080 fibrosarcoma cells; surface display confirmed by PI-PLC release of the GPI-anchored protein; no specific insertion residue is named in the paper.

sources.claim: In addition, a number of its biochemical features are both conflicting and controversial. To reassess the biochemical features of MT6-MMP, we have expressed the MT6-MMP construct tagged with a FLAG tag in breast carcinoma MCF-7 and fibrosarcoma HT1080 cells. We then used phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C to release MT6-MMP from the cell surface and characterized the solubilized MT6-MMP fractions. We now are confident that cellular MT6-MMP partially exists in its complex with TIMP-2. Both TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 are capable of inhibiting the proteolytic activity of MT6-MMP.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It reports a FLAG-tagged full-length GPI-anchored MT6-MMP (MMP25) construct that is surface-displayed and functionally active, but names no specific insertion residue. Because MMP25 is GPI-anchored (topology: SIGNAL 1–21, EXTRACELLULAR 22–562, no TM domain), the C-terminal GPI anchor signal precludes C-terminal tagging, leaving the mature N-terminus (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 21) as the sole extracellular terminus available. The position is therefore topology_derived. No internal loop insertions are reported in the ledger, and none are proposed. The paper confirms both surface display (PI-PLC release) and preserved function (TIMP-1/TIMP-2 inhibition, TIMP-2 complex formation), supporting a surface_and_function validation level.
